belief: One setback means I've ruined my life.
origins: A single event, such as a failed business, a layoff, a lost promotion, or a bad financial decision, can feel like proof that everything is ruined. This is especially strong when we have worked hard to avoid mistakes. Perfectionism, a family that punished failure, or a past experience in which one mistake had large consequences can make every setback feel final.
teaches: Scripture says that God works all things together for the good of those who love Him. Joseph told his brothers that what they intended for evil, God intended for good. Paul says we are persecuted but not forsaken, struck down but not destroyed. God said, “Do not call to mind the former things,” and “Behold, I am about to do something new.” These verses do not call a setback good. They say that it is not the last word, and that God can bring something out of it that we cannot yet see.
self_statements: There is no coming back from this.
errors: Turning one event into total ruin.
Seeing life as either perfect or ruined.
Treating one setback as a pattern for my whole life.
Seeing only the damage and missing what remains.
questions: What exactly was lost, and what is still here?
Has anyone I admire had a major setback and gone on to good things?
What did I learn that I could not have learned another way?
What parts of my life are untouched by this?
What might God be doing that I cannot yet see?
What is one thing I can rebuild first?
truth: A setback is real, but it is not my whole life. God can work through hard things, and nothing is wasted in His hands. I can grieve what was lost, keep what remains, and begin again.
hw_truths: A setback is not a ruined life.
God works all things together for good.
What remains is worth building on.
I do not have to see the whole plan.
One chapter is not the whole book.
log: Each week, list one thing lost and one thing that remains. Notice how the lists compare.
actions: Write what was lost and what remains. Include people, skills, faith, and health.
Write two lessons you can take forward.
Pick one area and take one small action this week.
Tell a trusted friend what happened and what you hope to do next.
prayer: Lord, this setback feels huge. Remind me that it is not the end of my story. Work in this for good, show me what remains, and give me courage to begin again. Amen.
hw_questions: What was lost and what remains?
What parts of my life are untouched?
Who has come back from a setback?
What is one thing to rebuild first?
name_example: Sarah can write: “God works all things together for good, so this setback is not the end of my story.”
